title: "Quantification"
format:

A missing precursor usually means it was too faint to detect, not that it was absent at random.
limpa turns that into a model in two steps. `dpc()` fits one detection probability curve for the
whole experiment: the chance a precursor is detected, given how abundant it is. `dpcQuant()` then
gives every protein a value and a standard error in every biopsy, using its observed precursors
and, through the curve, what its missing ones imply. Nothing is filled in as if measured; a value
resting on few detections carries a wide standard error, and later fits weight it less.

After quantification this step builds the blood index, removes contaminant proteins and keeps
proteins detected often enough to compare.

## Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(limma)
library(limpa)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
step <- here("01_Processing", "02_Quantification")
inputs <- c(
  precursors = "01_Processing/01_Precursors/c_data/precursors.rds",
  contaminants = "01_Processing/02_Quantification/references/contaminants.csv"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
```

## Input

The precursor matrix from `01_Precursors`: log2 intensities, `NA` where undetected, one column
per biopsy.

```{r}
#| label: input
y <- readRDS(paths[["precursors"]])
c(precursors = nrow(y), proteins = n_distinct(y$genes$Protein.Group), biopsies = ncol(y))
```

## Detection probability curve

The curve is logistic: P(detected | log2 intensity y) = plogis(β0 + β1 y). The slope β1 says how
strongly detection depends on abundance; 0 would mean values go missing at random. limpa's
authors report slopes of about 0.7 to 1 in real data. The curve is fitted on every precursor,
contaminants included, because it describes the instrument's detection of any precursor.

```{r}
#| label: dpc
dpcest <- dpc(y)
dpcest$dpc
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dpc
#| fig-cap: "Detection probability against log2 intensity (limpa's plotDPC)."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
plotDPC(dpcest)
```

## Quantify proteins

`dpcQuant()` fits each protein's precursors together (protein level plus a fixed offset per
precursor), with the missing ones entering through the curve and a prior estimated from all
proteins. It returns complete log2 values in `E`, a standard error per value in
`other$standard.error`, and per protein the precursor count (`NPrec`) and the share of values
observed (`PropObs`).

```{r}
#| label: quantify
proteins <- dpcQuant(y, "Protein.Group", dpc = dpcest)
c(proteins = nrow(proteins), biopsies = ncol(proteins), missing = sum(is.na(proteins$E)))
```

How much each protein rests on: precursors per protein and the share of its values observed.

```{r}
#| label: support
proteins$genes |>
  as_tibble() |>
  summarise(
    proteins = n(), one_precursor = sum(NPrec == 1), median_precursors = median(NPrec),
    median_observed = round(median(PropObs), 2), observed_under_half = sum(PropObs < 0.5)
  )
quantile(proteins$other$standard.error, c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))
```

Standard errors grow as fewer values are observed:

```{r}
#| label: fig-se
#| fig-cap: "Median standard error per protein against the share of its values observed."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
tibble(
  observed = proteins$genes$PropObs,
  se = apply(proteins$other$standard.error, 1, median)
) |>
  ggplot(aes(observed, se)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = "share of values observed", y = "median standard error") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

## Samples

`plotMDSUsingSEs()` (limpa) places biopsies by their protein values, like limma's `plotMDS`, but
takes the standard errors into account. Colour is time point, label the biopsy.

```{r}
#| label: fig-mds
#| fig-cap: "Multidimensional scaling of the biopsies (limpa's plotMDSUsingSEs)."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
tp_colour <- c(T1 = "#1B9E77", T2 = "#D95F02", T3 = "#7570B3")
mds <- plotMDSUsingSEs(
  proteins,
  labels = colnames(proteins), col = tp_colour[proteins$targets$timepoint], cex = 0.7
)
round(mds$var.explained[1:2], 3)
```

## Blood index

Blood in a biopsy dilutes the muscle proteins. The index is each biopsy's mean log2 HBB and HBA1,
taken from limpa's complete values, centred on the mean biopsy. Comparisons carry it as a
covariate.

```{r}
#| label: blood
blood_rows <- grepl("(^|;)(HBB|HBA1)(;|$)", proteins$genes$Genes)
proteins$genes[blood_rows, c("Genes", "NPrec", "PropObs")]
stopifnot(sum(blood_rows) >= 2)
blood <- colMeans(proteins$E[blood_rows, , drop = FALSE])
proteins$targets$blood <- unname(blood - mean(blood))
blood_index <- proteins$targets |>
  as_tibble() |>
  select(sample_id, subject, group, timepoint, blood)
summary(blood_index$blood)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-blood
#| fig-cap: "Blood index per biopsy by time point and group."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3
ggplot(blood_index, aes(timepoint, blood, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, seed = 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "blood index (centred log2)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10)
```

## Contaminants

`references/contaminants.csv` holds the 222 contaminant proteins the earlier protein-level pipeline
resolved (plasma, immunoglobulin, erythrocyte, keratin, complement, globin, leukocyte; see
`references/README.md`). They are removed now, after quantification: each protein is quantified
from its own precursors, so removing them afterwards leaves every other protein's values
unchanged apart from the shared prior.

```{r}
#| label: contaminants
contaminants <- readr::read_csv(paths[["contaminants"]], show_col_types = FALSE)
removed <- contaminants |>
  filter(uniprot_id %in% rownames(proteins)) |>
  arrange(class, gene)
count(removed, class)
c(on_list = nrow(contaminants), present = nrow(removed))
proteins <- proteins[!rownames(proteins) %in% contaminants$uniprot_id, ]
nrow(proteins)
```

Proteins not on the list cannot be removed by it. Remaining keratin, immunoglobulin and haemoglobin
genes, printed for review and kept:

```{r}
#| label: review
review <- proteins$genes |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "uniprot_id") |>
  filter(grepl("(^|;)(KRT|IG[HKL]|HB[ABDGQ])", Genes)) |>
  select(uniprot_id, gene = Genes, n_precursors = NPrec, prop_observed = PropObs)
review
```

## Detection filter

`filterByDetection()` (limpa) keeps proteins with at least one observed precursor in at least
`n.samples` biopsies. Its help page suggests the smallest group size for a small study; each
group-by-time cell holds 8 biopsies, so a kept protein was detected in at least one cell's worth of
biopsies (decisions log, 2026-10-15). It runs after quantification, as limpa intends: the curve
and the prior use every precursor.

```{r}
#| label: detection
detected <- filterByDetection(proteins, n.samples = 8)
table(kept = detected)
dropped <- proteins$genes[!detected, ] |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "uniprot_id") |>
  select(uniprot_id, gene = Genes, n_precursors = NPrec, prop_observed = PropObs)
proteins <- proteins[detected, ]
c(proteins = nrow(proteins), one_precursor = sum(proteins$genes$NPrec == 1))
```

## Protein values per biopsy

The same check as for precursors, now on limpa's complete protein values: one curve per biopsy,
which should overlap.

```{r}
#| label: fig-protein-densities
#| fig-cap: "log2 protein values per biopsy (limma's plotDensities)."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
plotDensities(proteins, legend = FALSE, main = "")
round(summary(apply(proteins$E, 2, median)), 2)
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(proteins$E), all(proteins$other$standard.error > 0),
  identical(colnames(proteins), proteins$targets$sample_id),
  !any(rownames(proteins) %in% contaminants$uniprot_id), !anyNA(proteins$targets$blood)
)
```

## Summary

`r nrow(proteins)` proteins in `r ncol(proteins)` biopsies, after removing `r nrow(removed)`
contaminants and `r nrow(dropped)` proteins detected in fewer than 8 biopsies. The detection
curve's slope is `r round(dpcest$dpc[2], 2)`; `r sum(proteins$genes$NPrec == 1)` kept proteins rest
on a single precursor.

## Save

`quantification.rds` is limpa's `EList`: `E`, `other$standard.error`, `genes` and `targets` with the
blood index. `dpcDE()` in the comparisons reads it directly.

```{r}
#| label: save
out <- file.path(step, "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(proteins, file.path(out, "quantification.rds"))
write_workbook(
  list(
    dpc = tibble(term = names(dpcest$dpc), estimate = unname(dpcest$dpc)),
    proteins = as_tibble(proteins$genes, rownames = "uniprot_id") |>
      select(
        uniprot_id, protein_name = Protein.Names, gene = Genes, n_precursors = NPrec,
        prop_observed = PropObs
      ),
    blood_index = blood_index,
    contaminants_removed = removed,
    contaminant_review = review,
    detection_dropped = dropped
  ),
  c(
    "Detection probability curve: intercept (beta0) and slope (beta1).",
    "Every protein kept: names, precursor count and share of values observed.",
    "Blood index per biopsy (centred mean log2 HBB and HBA1).",
    "Contaminant proteins removed, with class and reason.",
    "Keratin, immunoglobulin and haemoglobin genes not on the list, kept for review.",
    "Proteins detected in fewer than 8 biopsies, dropped by filterByDetection()."
  ),
  file.path(out, "quantification.xlsx"), inputs, paths
)
```
